candidates.name: LDPartEditor
candidates.why: The maintained editor for creating and fixing LDraw parts, the step no listed CAD (Studio, LeoCAD, LDCad) covers when a part is missing from the library.
candidates.rank_reason: Only active dedicated LDraw part editor (release v1.9.05 on 20 November 2026, Windows, Linux, macOS); listed on LDraw.org third-party software.

candidates.name: Web Lic
candidates.why: Browser-based instruction-book editor for LDraw models, a free alternative to LPub3D that needs no installation.
candidates.rank_reason: Second instruction-layout tool after LPub3D (already listed); 58 stars, last push 8 July 2026; smaller project, hence rank 2.

candidates.name: Brickit
candidates.why: Most used pile-scanning app: recognises loose bricks on a photo, keeps a digital inventory in numbered pockets and suggests builds; none of the listed apps scans a whole pile.
candidates.rank_reason: 23K App Store ratings, version 5.8.4 on 19 November 2026, 13 interface languages since 13 November 2026; also covers the inventory and sorting usage.

candidates.name: LEGO Powered Up app
candidates.why: Official LEGO app that drives Powered Up hubs, motors and trains and offers block coding for custom builds; the listed LEGO Builder app only shows instructions.
candidates.rank_reason: Official control app for current train and Powered Up sets (version 4.4.2 on 16 June 2026); fits apps and programming-and-control.

candidates.name: ImportLDraw (Blender add-on)
candidates.why: Reference way to render LDraw and Studio-exported models photorealistically in Blender; no listed entry covers rendering.
candidates.rank_reason: Most starred LDraw renderer (379 stars), version 1.3.0 on 5 October 2026 for Blender 4 and 5; alternative ldr_tools_blender (57 stars) left out.

candidates.name: LEGO.scad
candidates.why: Parametric OpenSCAD generator of compatible bricks, plates, tiles and Technic holes for 3D printing custom parts.
candidates.rank_reason: Reference 3D-printing generator (397 stars, MIT, last push 18 July 2026); Technic.scad by the same author is its companion.

candidates.name: MachineBlocks
candidates.why: Online and open-source editor that outputs 3MF or STL compatible bricks with a calibration tool for a printer's tolerances.
candidates.rank_reason: Newer than LEGO.scad (76 stars) but active (push 23 November 2026) and usable without OpenSCAD; ranks after LEGO.scad.

candidates.name: Eagle Animation
candidates.why: Free open-source stop-motion software from Brick a Brack, the association behind Brickfilms.com; brick films have no tool entry.
candidates.rank_reason: Active (push 24 November 2026, Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, web), French maintainers, tied to the main brick-film community.

candidates.name: buildinginstructions.js (BrickHub)
candidates.why: Renders LDraw building instructions step by step in a browser with three.js; powers BrickHub.org.
candidates.rank_reason: 149 stars, push 23 October 2026; library for developers, so last of the group.

candidates.name: pylgbst
candidates.why: Python library that drives Powered Up, Boost and Technic hubs over Bluetooth from a computer, without replacing the hub firmware as Pybricks does.
candidates.rank_reason: Most starred Powered Up library (587 stars), push 22 November 2026; complements node-poweredup (JavaScript) already listed.

candidates.name: Raspberry Pi Build HAT
candidates.why: Official Raspberry Pi board, made with LEGO Education, that runs SPIKE and Powered Up motors and sensors from Python.
candidates.rank_reason: Official hardware bridge between Raspberry Pi and current LEGO motors (LPF2 connector); operating product on sale.

candidates.name: LEGO Education SPIKE App
candidates.why: Official web and desktop app to program SPIKE Prime, SPIKE Essential and Robot Inventor hubs in blocks or Python.
candidates.rank_reason: Official programming environment of the current LEGO hubs; page reached today, version date not read.

candidates.name: SharpBrick PoweredUp (.NET)
candidates.why: .NET implementation of the LEGO Wireless Protocol, the counterpart of pylgbst and node-poweredup for C# developers.
candidates.rank_reason: 110 stars, push 6 June 2026; narrower audience than Python.

candidates.name: BrickPi3
candidates.why: Board and libraries that let a Raspberry Pi drive MINDSTORMS NXT and EV3 motors and sensors, keeping retired robotics kits useful.
candidates.rank_reason: 132 stars, push 17 November 2026; serves owners of discontinued MINDSTORMS kits.

candidates.name: HoMa's World of Bricks (Holger Matthes)
candidates.why: German reference on SNOT building and LEGO train modelling (wheels, 12 V trains, layouts) by the author of the book LEGO-Eisenbahnwelt, with a free English supplement.
candidates.rank_reason: Best German-language technique site found; regime work (guide), page updated after BSBT 2024, no precise date read.

candidates.name: ItLUG: unofficial guide to advanced LEGO building techniques
candidates.why: Authorised Italian translation of Didier Enjary's classic guide to advanced techniques (SNOT, offsets, ToPLESs), with a PDF; no Italian guide is listed.
candidates.rank_reason: Reference Italian technique guide (15313 downloads shown); regime work; itlug.org is listed as a club, this is a distinct usage at a distinct address.

candidates.name: MILS: Modular Integrated Landscaping System
candidates.why: Module standard for building shared dioramas and landscapes, approved by the HispaBrick Magazine team; counterpart for scenery of the listed L-Gauge Modular System.
candidates.rank_reason: Most cited Spanish-origin building standard (also in the ad-si awesome list); regime work; undated page.

candidates.name: Build Like a Master (official LEGO video series)
candidates.why: Official LEGO video course on brick anatomy, interlocking and SNOT, published in many languages, which fills the gap for languages without a fan guide.
candidates.rank_reason: Basics aimed at families, so last; kept because it is the only multilingual official technique course.

candidates.name: Supreme Court of Canada, Kirkbi AG v. Ritvik Holdings (2005 SCC 65)
candidates.why: Leading ruling that the stud pattern is purely functional and cannot be a trademark, which made Mega Bloks and other compatible bricks lawful in Canada.
candidates.rank_reason: Most quoted court decision on compatible bricks outside the EU; bilingual official text.

candidates.name: General Court of the EU, case T-515/19, Lego v EUIPO (building block design)
candidates.why: 2021 judgment holding that the modular-system exception can protect a LEGO brick design, the counterpart in design law of the listed trademark case C-48/09 P.
candidates.rank_reason: Main EU ruling after C-48/09 P; EUR-Lex returned an anti-robot answer (202), text read on BAILII.

candidates.name: Bundesgerichtshof, Klemmbausteine III (I ZR 30/02)
candidates.why: German Federal Court of Justice ruling of 2 December 2004 ending unfair-competition protection of the LEGO brick, the legal basis of the German Klemmbaustein market.
candidates.rank_reason: Only German-language legal source; Germany is the largest market of alternative brands in the directory.

candidates.name: Privy Council, Interlego AG v Tyco Industries (1988)
candidates.why: Privy Council ruling that redrawn LEGO design drawings gave no new copyright, which opened the way for Tyco Super Blocks and later compatible bricks.
candidates.rank_reason: Founding common-law case on brick copyright; the main BAILII address shows an anti-robot page, the text was read on its fast mirror.

candidates.name: The LEGO Story (Jens Andersen)
candidates.why: Authorised history of the LEGO Group written with access to its archives and to Kjeld Kirk Kristiansen; the listed history entries are web pages, not a full history.
candidates.rank_reason: Reference history book (432 pages, translated from Danish); regime work.

candidates.name: dpunkt.verlag: Lego & Co.

candidates.rank_reason: Largest German catalogue of unofficial LEGO books found (about ten titles); operating publisher.

coverage.tools: Complete meant: GitHub searched by stars with activity since 2025-11 (queries lego, topic:lego, ldraw, poweredup, mindstorms, spike prime, sorter, mosaic, technic, train, bricklink, rebrickable, studio, instructions), the ad-si/awesome-lego README (push 2026-11-02) and awesome-lego-machine-learning read, App Store searched for collection and official LEGO apps; only the leaders of each usage kept, the rest sent to the reference lists. Tools are international and almost all in English: no country- or language-specific tool reference was found for any perimeter country (German, French, Dutch apps all resolve to the international ones already listed). Uncertain: no new API or open data source qualified (Peeron and BrickLink catalog downloads resisted); inventory and sorting has no group of its own, Brickit carries it under apps; LEGO Technic CONTROL+ status unread.
coverage.learning: Complete meant: the official LCP list read in full (30 names) and compared with listed artists; FLL operators checked for the perimeter countries reached in one search (US/CA, GB, IT, NL, FI, DACH and FR already listed); leading rulings on compatible bricks read at source for CA, EU, DE and GB/HK; publisher catalogues looked for in DE, FR and IT; technique guides looked for in IT, ES and DE. Remaining gaps: guides and history for nl, pl, cs, da, sv, pt, no, fi; books for es, nl, pl; FLL operators for ES (unconfirmed), BE, PL, CZ, DK, SE, NO, PT, AU, NZ, ZA, IE, LU (use the FIRST partner list instead of entries); artists for PL (no site), ZA, NZ. Notes for the maintainer: (1) LEGO Education does not renew its partnership with FIRST: 2026-2027 BIOGLOW is the last joint season (Founders Edition last season 2027-2028), so the three listed FLL entries need a status note; (2) the current official LCP list no longer names Sean Kenney, Warren Elsmore or Ekow Nimako (Nathan Sawaya, Ryan McNaught, Georg Schmitt and Rene Hoffmeister are still on it), so their entries should not call them LCPs; (3) Brickfilms.com (active) is missing from the community category.

recommendation: Stop for tools: the remaining long tail belongs to the reference lists (LDraw software list, ad-si/awesome-lego, GitHub topic). For learning, one more short pass with Exa per missing language (nl, pl, cs, da, sv, pt) for guides and books, and the FIRST partner list for national FLL operators if the maintainer wants them as entries; Perplexity quota is exhausted (401 on 2026-11-24).
